title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: Price increase to $4.56 (+5.1%)
drivers.evidence: Two prior weeks at $4.56: medians 195 and 119 (x0.94 and x0.57 vs baseline). Noise-adjusted price effect: x0.75. No prior promotion at this price; price increase likely reduces demand.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 207.6. A 5.1% price increase to $4.56 (from $4.34) is significant, but no past promotion at this price point exists. The two prior weeks at $4.56 saw drops to 195 and 119 units (x0.94 and x0.57 vs baseline), suggesting strong price sensitivity. The heatwave (38°C) may boost demand for cold beverages, but milk is not a heat-driven impulse item. No event or promotion is scheduled. The classical uplift model's 1.00 multiplier is unconvincing given the price spike and historical response. The noise-adjusted price effect from prior $4.56 weeks is x0.75. Confidence is medium due to limited data on price response at this level.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 207.6 | 5%-95%: 133.4 - 290.4 | 10%-90%: 156.2 - 281.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
